name: azul_widgets_a_start_asks_the_app_for_its_dom_once_and_for_the_video_status_once
description: E76 (2026-11-28): a cold start asks the app's layout() for its DOM ONCE, and nothing the platform does after the first picture asks again (the window gaining the focus, the first resize event at the size the window has, the app becoming active, a thread being started). The QA's cold-start lab printed a second `layout_begin #N reason=RefreshDom` after the first picture of AzWidgets on every Android start (+7 ms), on every iOS Simulator start (+58 to 93 ms, right after applicationDidBecomeActive:) and, in the X11 timeline, +1 ms after it (the shell marked the DOM for regeneration to start polling the first thread): each ran the app's whole layout() again, 0.3 to 0.9 s of the engine's time on the emulator. What AzWidgets itself asks for after its first layout is ONE rebuild: the video card's status report (Loading -> Failed or Paused, `on_video_status` in examples/azul-widgets/src/video.rs) redraws its controls; that is the app's own callback answering RefreshDom, and the bound counts it. So: at most 2 DOM regenerations since the window opened (every file runs in a process of its own), after 2.5 s of nobody touching the app, which is more than the second layout takes where it still happens; when the video card updates its controls in place, the bound is 1.
